chapter: Will Marion Cook and the Southern Syncopated Orchestra
title: The orchestra splits: Cook's half versus Latimore's
summary: Cook refused to abandon his players, so half went with Latimore, who imported new performers, and half with Cook, whose unit failed on the road under a poor advance manager.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Sure. Okay, so then you got into this problem between Lattimore and the band, and the guys in the band all quit, I guess that's what happened.

Well, what happened, half the band quit. You see, we didn't -- we were divided into two parts because Dad Cook refused. He saw that Lattimore would take advantage of us. He probably offered Dad Cook a nice sum. But Dad was not the type of guy to leave his lambs, as he called us.
I see, he was protecting the boys.

Yes. He was protecting everybody. He tried to get Mr. Lattimore to be a little more reasonable, and after he found out that he couldn't, he told Lattimore, he said, 'Well, I'll go my way and you go your way.'
And half of us went with Latimore, and half went with Dad, and half went with Latimore.
Well, Latimore having all the money, he sent to America and brought other persons over. Singers and choirs and everything else. Musicians.
We, also, had gotten a few local talent that were pretty good.

We had English colored and mixed. And we went on, but we didn't have the finance behind us, that Latimore had. We went on the road and then now and then we had a very bad, what you'd call an advance manager.
He would spend the money living in big hotels, and going to cabarets and everything, and we'd get to a town and there was
no advertisement, nothing. No publicity, nothing.
And we had, what, eight, ten, weeks of that, and we then we were about to fold, we folded.
